rule.title: At-Fault Just Cause Grounds
rule.requirement: At-fault just cause is restricted to default in rent, lease breach after written notice to correct, maintaining a nuisance, waste, refusal to renew an expired lease on substantially similar terms, criminal activity on the premises, criminal threats directed at the landlord or another tenant, unlawful assignment or subletting, refusal of lawful landlord entry, unlawful use of the property, failure of an employee or agent to vacate upon termination of employment, or failure to deliver possession after tenant's notice to terminate or written offer to surrender.

[§98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law (California Civil Code sections 798-799.11) are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(g); document-wide]; Residential rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence there is exempt from this Division. rule.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants written notice in at least 12-point font stating that California law limits rent increases under Civil Code section 1947.12, local law requires a statement of cause to terminate, and seniors or disabled tenants may be entitled to additional protections.

A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide 
written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that 
complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that 
states as follows: 
California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See 
California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information. Local law 
also provides that a landlord shall provide a statement of cause in any 
notice to terminate a tenancy. In some circumstances, tenants who are 
seniors (62 years or older) or disabled may be entitled to additional 
tenant protections. See Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San 
Diego Municipal Code for more information.

rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies continuously occupying residential rental property for more than 30 days, excluding leases for a fixed term of three months or less. [§98.0702; document-wide]
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy, as defined in and subject to Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code, is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(b); document-wide]; Housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction, or other agreement with a government agency as affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, excluding Section 8 voucher tenancies. [§98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law (California Civil Code sections 798-799.11) are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(g); document-wide]; Residential rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence there is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(h); document-wide]; A single-family residence occupied by the landlord as their principal residence is exempt, including renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two JADUs, or a mobilehome. [§98.0703(i); document-wide]; A property containing two separate dwelling units within a single structure where the landlord occupies one unit as their principal residence from the beginning and continues in occupancy is exempt. [§98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt, unless it is a mobilehome. [§98.0703(k); document-wide]

this Division, a landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall 
render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.

rule.title: Wrongful Eviction Damages
rule.requirement: Any attempt or actual recovery of possession of a residential rental property in violation of this Division renders the landlord liable to the tenant for wrongful eviction damages of not less than three times actual economic damages.
rule.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies continuously occupying residential rental property for more than 30 days, excluding leases for a fixed term of three months or less. [§98.0702; document-wide]
rule.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy as defined in California Civil Code section 1940(b) is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(a); document-wide]; Short-term residential occupancy, as defined in and subject to Chapter 5, Article 10, Division 1 of the San Diego Municipal Code, is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(b); document-wide]; Housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction, or other agreement with a government agency as affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(c); document-wide]; Housing subject to an agreement providing subsidies for affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households is exempt, excluding Section 8 voucher tenancies. [§98.0703(d); document-wide]; Mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law (California Civil Code sections 798-799.11) are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(e); document-wide]; Housing accommodations in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(f); document-wide]; Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a K-12 school are exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(g); document-wide]; Residential rental property where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains their principal residence there is exempt from this Division. [§98.0703(h); document-wide]; A single-family residence occupied by the landlord as their principal residence is exempt, including renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs, or two JADUs, or a mobilehome. [§98.0703(i); document-wide]; A property containing two separate dwelling units within a single structure where the landlord occupies one unit as their principal residence from the beginning and continues in occupancy is exempt. [§98.0703(j); document-wide]; Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt, unless it is a mobilehome. [§98.0703(k); document-wide]
